chunks: Hasten towards the common matter which is peculiar to every one; and that is death.

Certainly, people (who have already gone) are ahead of you while the hour (Day of Judgement) is driving you from behind. Remain light, in order that you may overtake them. Your backs are being awaited for the sake of the fronts.
Fear Allāh in the matter of His creatures and His cities because you will be questioned even about lands and beasts.
Obey Allāh and do not disobey Him. When you see virtue adopt it, and when you see vice avoid it.
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about hastening towards death and accountability for creation?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of the Hour driving believers from behind to emphasize the urgency of preparing for the inevitable end, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatological reflection on the transient nature of worldly life. The emphasis on accountability extending to 'lands and beasts' highlights the comprehensive scope of divine justice, a theme often cited in Shia jurisprudence regarding environmental stewardship and the rights of non-human creatures. This advice serves as a practical guide for balancing spiritual readiness with ethical conduct in daily interactions with creation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Hasten towards the most common matter which is peculiar to every one; and that is death.

Certainly, people (who have already gone) are ahead of you while the hour (Day of Judgement) is driving you from behind. Remain light, in order that you may overtake them. Your backs are being awaited for the sake of the fronts.
Fear Allāh in the matter of His creatures and His cities because you will be questioned even about lands and beasts.
Obey Allāh and do not disobey Him. When you see virtue adopt it, and when you see vice avoid it.
